title: Ice creep, animated - and yes, the weather warmed up
question: Now that it moves: does the freeze creep at a rate that feels right, and does the thaw at the end read as the weather turning rather than as ice vanishing?
context_md:
You said: *"Not sure on timing without an animated gif or playtest but the pattern looks good. It does disappear after the 3rd panel. Did the weather warm up?"*

**Yes.** It was not a bug and it was not the ice giving up -- the cold snap ends. Counted across the same run:

| step | frozen cells | snow cells |
|---|---|---|
| 600 | 375 | 1,577 |
| 700 | 362 | 1,788 |
| **800** | **0** | **0** |

The snow turns to rain at world frame 25,010, which is step 700 of this run -- and that fell exactly between my third and fourth stills, so the sheet showed you a full pond and then an empty one with nothing in between to say why. That is my fault for using stills on a timing question when the tool has done animation all along.

This clip is 100 frames at step 600 to 1,200, so it brackets the thaw: you should see the sheet at its widest, then go. Cropped to the pond and its two shores.

Nothing about the ice changed since your last look -- this is the same behaviour, shown properly.

items.label: cold snap into thaw
items.caption: Steps 600-1200. Snow turns to rain at step 700; frozen cells go 375 -> 362 -> 0.
